## Summary (human-written)
<!-- Write this yourself, not with an AI tool. 2-5 sentences: the problem, why
     this approach, and what you checked yourself. -->

## Agent details

Stacked on #5543 ("[MoE] Apply router scores before W2 projection"). Please review only the top commit.

**TLDR:** With DeepEP, the activation output is multiplied by the router scores before w2, as a separate eager op. This PR moves the multiply into the activation's compiled kernel: fp32 math, one rounding, no extra pass over the `[R, F]` activation (R = rows routed to this rank, F = expert hidden size). Activation plus multiply gets about 3x faster. Today only the debug recipe `qwen3_moe_deepep` takes this path: the DeepEP RL recipes use `fused_swiglu` (NOTE).

```text
multiply after activation:   w13 -> activation -> * scores (eager, bf16) -> w2 -> combine (sum)
multiply inside activation:  w13 -> activation with * scores (fp32)      -> w2 -> combine (sum)
```

**Solution**
1. `BinaryActivationFn.__call__` (base of SwiGLU, LimitedSwiGLU, ClampedSwiGLU, SiTUGLU) takes `scores` (`[R]` or None). The compiled region computes `(hidden * scores[:, None]).to(bf16)`.
2. `RoutedExperts` passes the DeepEP scores, and None for other dispatchers.
3. `FusedSwiGLU` accepts `scores` but keeps the separate bf16 multiply: its Triton kernels take no scores.

**Results** (one production-size MoE layer, EP 2, 2x GB300, arms run back to back)

```text
Numerics: not bitwise. Activation output vs fp64 (R = 4096, F = 768):
          after 2.78e-3 | inside 1.66e-3 | one bf16 rounding 1.66e-3

rel L2 vs main (combine scales), compiled: output / input grad / worst weight grad
             multiply after       multiply inside      yardstick
Qwen3        4.8 / 5.8 / 4.6e-3   5.6 / 6.2 / 4.7e-3   5.3 / 5.6 / 5.0e-3
DeepSeek-V3  3.8 / 4.5 / 4.6e-3   4.4 / 4.8 / 4.7e-3   5.1 / 5.1 / 5.0e-3
Qwen3.5      3.3 / 4.3 / 4.6e-3   3.8 / 4.5 / 4.6e-3   5.3 / 6.1 / 6.0e-3
```
- Yardstick: main eager vs main compiled. All cells are within 1.1x of it. Two Qwen3 cells are above it: output 5.6 vs 5.3e-3, input grad 6.2 vs 5.6e-3 (multiply after: 5.8e-3).
- Bitwise, one layer: reruns, default remat vs no remat, CUDA-graph replay vs the same forward without capture, the new kernel's grad vs no-grad forward (op level), and `fused_swiglu` vs multiply after.
- End to end, `qwen3_moe_deepep` (FSDP 2 x EP 2, 30 steps), worst rel diff in loss / grad norm: inside vs main 1.0e-4 / 2.6e-3, after vs main 3.0e-4 / 1.4e-2.
- Main run twice differs as much: 4.0e-4 / 1.4e-2. This recipe is not bitwise run to run, even with `debug.deterministic`. So end to end shows no difference beyond that noise.

```text
us, after -> inside (tokens per rank)   Qwen3       DeepSeek-V3   Qwen3.5
activation + multiply, fwd+bwd, 16k     803 -> 276  2070 -> 683   546 -> 183
MoE layer, CUDA-graph replay, 2048      457 -> 394  2740 -> 2602  473 -> 428
```
- Training saves about 2.6-4.2% of the layer's compiled fwd+bwd step (16k tokens per rank, no remat). Layer step times were too noisy to show it (identical code moved 23% between runs).
- Memory: unchanged with default remat. Without remat, with compile regions: one fewer bf16 `[R, F]` per layer.

You may ask: **Why not a compiled multiply in `RoutedExperts`?** A second region is a second kernel: the extra pass this PR removes.

NOTE:
- Dropping `fused_swiglu` from the DeepEP RL recipes would move them here. At 16k tokens per rank that saves activation + multiply time, about 2-4% of the layer's compiled fwd+bwd step with `fused_swiglu`, no remat (Qwen3 0.57 of 13.6 ms, DeepSeek-V3 1.41 of 41.9 ms, Qwen3.5 0.35 of 18.9 ms). That needs an RL run: follow-up.
- The forward stays batch invariant (RL logprob parity unchanged). The backward does not: each row's score gradient depends on its position. Without `debug.deterministic`, router grads differ in the last bits from run to run.
- Only SwiGLU was measured.
- Without compile regions, the fp32 multiply raises peak memory (Qwen3, 16k tokens per rank: +0.44 GiB).

**Test plan**
- `test_scores_scale_rows_in_one_kernel` (new) and `test_matches_reference_forward_and_backward` (now with scores) fail if the multiply is broken.
- GPU: `test_swiglu.py`, `test_fused_swiglu_override.py`, `test_situglu.py` 18 passed; `test_deepep_activation_checkpoint.py` (2 GPUs) 2 passed. CPU: models/common, recipes, RL 893 passed, 1 failed (`test_lora_forward`, fails the same without this PR's commit). pre-commit, pyrefly clean.

nodes.body:
**Claude finished @felipemello1's task in 2m 53s** —— [View job](https://github.com/pytorch/torchtitan/actions/runs/41597259345)

---
**Approve -- please address the items before merging** (the human-written summary is empty, plus one docstring nit). See the [review](https://github.com/pytorch/torchtitan/pull/5765#pullrequestreview).

Reply from claude: This PR is not in the MoE stack on purpose. It is built on #5543 (another author's PR, under review). Linking it on top of #5708 would make it wait for 5 PRs and carry #5543's commits. Once #5543 lands, I'll rebase this onto the top of the stack and link it.
No other open PR applies the router scores inside the activation. Megatron-LM's `weighted_swiglu` does the same: it computes `swiglu(y) * weights` and casts once.

**Verdict: Approve -- please address the items below before merging** -- the top commit (599361c) is a small change in the right place. It removes one eager pass and one bf16 rounding on the DeepEP path, and every other path builds the same graph as before. A maintainer still needs to review, since this touches `models/common/`.

**What this PR does.** With DeepEP, the router-score multiply used to run as a separate eager op after the activation. Now `BinaryActivationFn.__call__` takes an optional `scores=[R]` and does the multiply inside the `fused_binary_activation` compiled region, in fp32, with a single cast to bf16. `RoutedExperts` passes the DeepEP scores and `None` for every other dispatcher. `FusedSwiGLU` takes `scores` but keeps the old bf16 multiply after its Triton op, so that path's math is unchanged.

**Example.** DeepEP, `R` routed rows, fp32 `routed_scores_R`:
```text
before: h = swiglu(gate_up)                       # compiled, bf16 out (round 1)
        h = h * scores.to(bf16)[:, None]          # eager pass, scores round, product rounds
after:  h = swiglu(gate_up, scores=scores)        # one kernel: silu(g)*u*s in fp32, round once
Local/AllToAll dispatchers: scores=None -> same Dynamo graph as before (guarded on None).
fused_swiglu recipes: hidden * scores.to(hidden.dtype) -> same math as before.
```

### Must fix
1. PR description -- the "Summary (human-written)" section is empty. The author needs to fill it in; agents can't do that.

### Should consider
- `torchtitan/models/common/activation.py:64` -- the "rounds once" claim doesn't hold for `SiTUGLU` (see inline).
- `torchtitan_recipes/overrides/fused_swiglu.py:343` -- the speedup doesn't reach any production recipe until the RL recipes stop using `fused_swiglu` (see the TODO). That's fine as a follow-up, but the description should say plainly that the only consumer today is the debug recipe `qwen3_moe_deepep`. It already says this under the TLDR, so this is just a note for the maintainer.

<details><summary>Details</summary>

- **Gate.** The problem is real: an extra `[R, F]` pass plus a double rounding. The layer is right too: the activation region is the only place the multiply fuses without adding a second compiled region. Nothing in `direction.md` or any open PR supersedes it. Net LoC for this commit is +81, almost all of it tests.
- **Callsites.** `activation_fn(...)` is called in `moe.py` (updated), `feed_forward.py`, and `qwen3_5/moe.py`. The last two are dense and don't pass scores. `BinaryActivationFn.__call__` is overridden only by `FusedSwiGLU` (updated). `Dist-MoE` and `gpt_oss` don't call the base activation with scores. `_SelectGate` in the CPU MoE test is the only test stub that needed the new kwarg.
- **Remat.** The activation is a bare (non-region) op that reads the dispatch region's scores, so keeping `recompute_needs_tensor(routed_scores_R)` is correct.
- **Batch invariance.** `batch_invariant=True` is still accurate for the forward. The backward with scores is not batch invariant, as the new comment says. `rl/BITWISE_PARITY.md` only claims forward (logprob) parity, and batch-invariant mode requires `deterministic=True`, so nothing that relies on parity regresses. The existing `test_forward_and_backward_are_batch_invariant` still covers only the no-scores case, which is the correct scope.
- **Eager fallback** (region disabled): the multiply now builds a transient fp32 `[R, F]` tensor, which is the +0.44 GiB peak noted in the description. That's acceptable under "don't optimize eager fallbacks".
- **Tests.** The `FusedSwiGLU` scores subtest guards the only override. The kernel-count assertion guards the perf claim. Both earn their place.

</details>

Not verified: the GPU numerics, kernel-count, and timing claims. I didn't run anything.

"Rounds once" isn't true for every subclass. `SiTUGLU._activation_fn` ends with `.to(input_dtype)`, so its hidden is already rounded to bf16 before the score multiply, and the result is rounded again. That makes two roundings, the same as the old multiply-after path. This only matters if someone uses Kimi K3 with DeepEP, but this base-class docstring is the contract. Smallest fix: scope the claim, e.g. "the compiled region multiplies in fp32 and rounds once, unless `_activation_fn` itself casts to a lower dtype (SiTUGLU does)". Or drop SiTUGLU's trailing cast so it returns fp32 and the base does the single cast. That second option changes SiTUGLU's numerics for every caller, so the wording fix is the safer one here.

nodes.body: Reply from claude: Inside the compiled region, SiTUGLU still rounds once. Inductor drops a downcast-upcast pair between fused ops, so SiTUGLU's `.to(input_dtype)` stays in fp32 inside the kernel. The `emulate_precision_casts` comment in `torch/_inductor/config.py` describes this. That knob keeps the casts, and it is off by default (`TORCHINDUCTOR_EMULATE_PRECISION_CASTS=0`). A CPU probe at 599361c31 agrees: compiled SiTUGLU with scores has the error of one bf16 rounding vs fp64. Without compile regions, SiTUGLU's own cast does round first. The docstring scopes the claim to "the compiled region" for that reason.

+class _PostW2(_DeepEPBlock):
+    """Reference DeepEP experts with router scores applied after W2."""
+
+    def forward(self, x_TD: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
+        num_tokens = x_TD.shape[0]
+        token_ids_T1 = torch.arange(num_tokens, device=x_TD.device).unsqueeze(-1)
+        offsets_1K = torch.arange(_TOP_K, device=x_TD.device).unsqueeze(0)
+        expert_ids_TK = (token_ids_T1 + offsets_1K) % self.num_experts
+        # Scores depend on the gate, so the router gets a gradient too.
+        scores_TK = torch.sigmoid(self.gate(x_TD)).gather(1, expert_ids_TK)
+        routing_map_TE = torch.zeros(
+            num_tokens, self.num_experts, dtype=torch.bool, device=x_TD.device
+        ).scatter_(1, expert_ids_TK, True)
+        experts = self.routed_experts
+        routed_RD, counts_E, metadata = experts.token_dispatcher.dispatch(
+            x_TD, scores_TK, expert_ids_TK, routing_map_TE
+        )
+        offsets_E = counts_E.cumsum(dim=0, dtype=torch.int32)
+        gate_up_R2F = experts.w13(routed_RD, offsets_E)
+        hidden_RF = experts.activation_fn(gate_up_R2F, offsets=offsets_E)
+        routed_output_RD = experts.w2(hidden_RF, offsets_E)
+        routed_output_RD = routed_output_RD * metadata.routed_scores_R.to(
+            routed_output_RD.dtype
+        ).reshape(-1, 1)
+        out_TD = experts.token_dispatcher.combine(
+            routed_output_RD,
+            metadata,
+            x_TD,
+        )
+        remat.recompute_needs_tensor(out_TD)
+        return out_TD.float().square().sum()
+
+

inline_comments.body: "Rounds once" isn't true for every subclass. `SiTUGLU._activation_fn` ends with `.to(input_dtype)`, so its hidden is already rounded to bf16 before the score multiply, and the result is rounded again. That makes two roundings, the same as the old multiply-after path. This only matters if someone uses Kimi K3 with DeepEP, but this base-class docstring is the contract. Smallest fix: scope the claim, e.g. "the compiled region multiplies in fp32 and rounds once, unless `_activation_fn` itself casts to a lower dtype (SiTUGLU does)". Or drop SiTUGLU's trailing cast so it returns fp32 and the base does the single cast. That second option changes SiTUGLU's numerics for every caller, so the wording fix is the safer one here.

inline_comments.body: Reply from claude: Inside the compiled region, SiTUGLU still rounds once. Inductor drops a downcast-upcast pair between fused ops, so SiTUGLU's `.to(input_dtype)` stays in fp32 inside the kernel. The `emulate_precision_casts` comment in `torch/_inductor/config.py` describes this. That knob keeps the casts, and it is off by default (`TORCHINDUCTOR_EMULATE_PRECISION_CASTS=0`). A CPU probe at 599361c31 agrees: compiled SiTUGLU with scores has the error of one bf16 rounding vs fp64. Without compile regions, SiTUGLU's own cast does round first. The docstring scopes the claim to "the compiled region" for that reason.

reviews.body:
**Verdict: Approve -- please address the items below before merging** -- the top commit (599361c) is a small change in the right place. It removes one eager pass and one bf16 rounding on the DeepEP path, and every other path builds the same graph as before. A maintainer still needs to review, since this touches `models/common/`.

**What this PR does.** With DeepEP, the router-score multiply used to run as a separate eager op after the activation. Now `BinaryActivationFn.__call__` takes an optional `scores=[R]` and does the multiply inside the `fused_binary_activation` compiled region, in fp32, with a single cast to bf16. `RoutedExperts` passes the DeepEP scores and `None` for every other dispatcher. `FusedSwiGLU` takes `scores` but keeps the old bf16 multiply after its Triton op, so that path's math is unchanged.

**Example.** DeepEP, `R` routed rows, fp32 `routed_scores_R`:
```text
before: h = swiglu(gate_up)                       # compiled, bf16 out (round 1)
        h = h * scores.to(bf16)[:, None]          # eager pass, scores round, product rounds
after:  h = swiglu(gate_up, scores=scores)        # one kernel: silu(g)*u*s in fp32, round once
Local/AllToAll dispatchers: scores=None -> same Dynamo graph as before (guarded on None).
fused_swiglu recipes: hidden * scores.to(hidden.dtype) -> same math as before.
```

### Must fix
1. PR description -- the "Summary (human-written)" section is empty. The author needs to fill it in; agents can't do that.

### Should consider
- `torchtitan/models/common/activation.py:64` -- the "rounds once" claim doesn't hold for `SiTUGLU` (see inline).
- `torchtitan_recipes/overrides/fused_swiglu.py:343` -- the speedup doesn't reach any production recipe until the RL recipes stop using `fused_swiglu` (see the TODO). That's fine as a follow-up, but the description should say plainly that the only consumer today is the debug recipe `qwen3_moe_deepep`. It already says this under the TLDR, so this is just a note for the maintainer.

<details><summary>Details</summary>

- **Gate.** The problem is real: an extra `[R, F]` pass plus a double rounding. The layer is right too: the activation region is the only place the multiply fuses without adding a second compiled region. Nothing in `direction.md` or any open PR supersedes it. Net LoC for this commit is +81, almost all of it tests.
- **Callsites.** `activation_fn(...)` is called in `moe.py` (updated), `feed_forward.py`, and `qwen3_5/moe.py`. The last two are dense and don't pass scores. `BinaryActivationFn.__call__` is overridden only by `FusedSwiGLU` (updated). `Dist-MoE` and `gpt_oss` don't call the base activation with scores. `_SelectGate` in the CPU MoE test is the only test stub that needed the new kwarg.
- **Remat.** The activation is a bare (non-region) op that reads the dispatch region's scores, so keeping `recompute_needs_tensor(routed_scores_R)` is correct.
- **Batch invariance.** `batch_invariant=True` is still accurate for the forward. The backward with scores is not batch invariant, as the new comment says. `rl/BITWISE_PARITY.md` only claims forward (logprob) parity, and batch-invariant mode requires `deterministic=True`, so nothing that relies on parity regresses. The existing `test_forward_and_backward_are_batch_invariant` still covers only the no-scores case, which is the correct scope.
- **Eager fallback** (region disabled): the multiply now builds a transient fp32 `[R, F]` tensor, which is the +0.44 GiB peak noted in the description. That's acceptable under "don't optimize eager fallbacks".
- **Tests.** The `FusedSwiGLU` scores subtest guards the only override. The kernel-count assertion guards the perf claim. Both earn their place.

</details>
